questions.q: Who were the children who came to play and ride Merrylegs?
choices: The vicar Mr. Blomefield's children
The squire's nephews
Children from London
John Manly's children
questions.evidence: Mr. Blomefield, the vicar, had a large family of boys and girls

questions.q: What did Merrylegs do to the boys who rode him too long?
choices: He pitched them off backward
He bit them
He kicked them
He ran home without them
questions.evidence: I just pitched them off backward

questions.q: How did Merrylegs treat the little children who were frightened on his back?
choices: He went smooth and quiet until they were all right
He galloped faster to make them brave
He refused to let them ride
He threw them off gently
questions.evidence: I go as smooth and as quiet as old pussy when she is after a bird

questions.q: What did the boys use as riding-whips?
choices: Hazel sticks they had cut
Their belts
James's whip
Long pieces of rope
questions.evidence: They had each cut a great hazel stick for a riding-whip

questions.q: What did Merrylegs mean when he said boys think a pony is like a steam-engine?
choices: They think a pony never gets tired and has no feelings
They think a pony is very fast
They think a pony makes loud noises
They think a pony is made of metal
questions.evidence: they never think that a pony can get tired, or have any feelings

questions.q: What did Merrylegs do before he finally made the boys slip off?
choices: He stopped two or three times as a hint
He bit the boy's foot
He ran into the stable
He lay down in the grass
questions.evidence: I stopped two or three times by way of a hint

questions.q: Why did Merrylegs refuse to kick the boys as Ginger said she would have done?
choices: He did not want to anger the master or make James ashamed
He was too old and weak to kick
He was afraid of the boys
He did not know how to kick
questions.evidence: as to anger our master or make James ashamed of me

questions.q: What did Merrylegs mean by "good places make good horses"?
choices: Horses that are treated kindly become good and trustworthy
Horses need big fields to grow strong
Only expensive stables are good
Horses should never be ridden by children
